### Read the Bible: Genesis 50, Luke 3, Job 16–17, 1 Corinthians 4
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-50-luke-3-job-16-17-1-corinthians-4/
Passage: Job 16:2
Points:
- Job felt further injured by companions who offered long-winded speeches instead of genuine comfort.
- True theological doctrines can wound deeply when applied insensitively, at the wrong time, or with condescension.
- Believers must evaluate their own attitudes to avoid using Scripture to oppress rather than heal.
- Desperate laments and complaints can still belong to a faithful believer striving to make sense of suffering.

### How to Be a Miserable Comforter: Two Ways We Fail the Hurting
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/how-to-be-a-miserable-comforter
Passage: Job 16:2
Points:
- Job rightly characterized his friends as miserable comforters because their theological diagnoses caused more damage.
- Counselors frequently fail the hurting by misapplying true doctrines to trials not caused by corrective discipline.
- Words spoken out of acute pain represent cries for relief rather than rebellious theological convictions.
- Wise comforters are slow to diagnose, quick to listen, and eager to restore wounded souls with patient love.

### How to Discourage a Grieving Friend
Author: Vaneetha Rendall Risner
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/how-to-discourage-a-grieving-friend
Passage: Job 16:2-5
Points:
- Hurting individuals are often discouraged when friends offer sermonettes and trite answers instead of presence.
- Job pleaded with his companions to stop their windy criticisms and instead offer words that relieve sorrow.
- Sufferers should not be pressured to suppress tears or maintain an appearance of theological composure.
- True encouragement comes from quietly sitting with friends in grief and pointing them gently to God's grace.

### Mourning Without Words
Author: Trillia Newbell
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/mourning-without-words/
Passage: Job 16:2
Points:
- Hurting friends are flesh-and-blood people needing love, not problems to be repaired with quick advice.
- Job's friends became miserable comforters the moment they spoke without waiting and thinking carefully.
- Practicing silent presence and shared tears is often far more helpful than rushing to offer explanations.
- Believers can embrace their own lack of answers and trust the God of comfort to sustain the brokenhearted.
